summary:
Both items were answered as asked, and the session made no claims. The plan exists (evidence/phase-diagram-plan.md), covers every point the instruction listed, and the sweep was not started. Option four was paused: no method branch or worktree was touched last night, and the stopped queue was not restarted (its log ends at 15:17 on November 13). program check passes; the latest approval is still Chris's from November 6. All 525 files listed in the five new evidence files match their recorded size and checksum.

Four things in the plan Chris should know before approving it.

(1) 'A phase diagram for each' is uneven in three dimensions. The no-friction engine gets onset loops at three frequencies, a scan above onset at six frequencies and long runs at all seven Figure 1 conditions. The nudge gets long runs at the five Figure 1 conditions not yet run and, last and only if the two-dimensional stage goes well, onset loops at two frequencies. There is no scan in Gamma for the nudge in three dimensions. The summary's 'a phase diagram for each engine in three dimensions at six frequencies' is true only of the no-friction engine. The reason is cost (the nudge costs three times as much, and far more below Gamma 2.5), which is fair, but it is a choice about what was asked and is not listed as one. Three dimensions also has one depth only (5.42).

(2) The budget question is answered by Chris's own file. budgets.yaml says the 400 CPU-hours are per week, and program check counts 208 of 400 this week (52 percent). The session reported 242 of 400, which is the total since November 5, and asked which it is. On the weekly reading about 190 hours are left this week.

(3) The 22 CPU-hours for the first stage is firm only for the no-friction engine. The summary says the stage covers all three engines; the cost file prices only two, and says the baseline with friction 'costs what the nudge does' (the nudge share is 12 of the 22). The nudge's share uses its rate at Gamma 2.5 and above, but an onset loop goes down to where the pilot measured it 7 to 900 times slower (0.28 seconds a cycle at Gamma 2.25, 0.87 at 2.15, 36 at 2.1, against 0.04 at 2.4 and above). At depth 10 the nudge did not get through its first cycle at Gamma 2.0 or 2.5 from a standing start, and no ramp has been tried there. Per-step CPU caps bound the damage, so the stage is still cheap, but 22 is a lower figure, not an estimate.

(4) The transition-point rule cannot be applied to the engines with friction as written. It measures the flat level and its scatter from the steps at the low end of the ramp. In the pilot the nudge reached three flat steps and the baseline one or two before stopping, so there is little or nothing to measure the flat level from, and the up branch has to start from wherever the engine stopped. The plan names this risk but does not say what Gamma_down means in that case. The two-start test (hold one Gamma from a flat start and from a patterned start) is the right decisive check and does not depend on it.

What I checked and found sound. The one no-friction stall is real and repeatable: I reran it and it enters the slow stretch at the same point (cycle 10, phase 0.902209). I also ran three seeds the session did not (4, 5 and 6) at the same condition: all three completed 120 cycles with no slow stretch and a clean audit. So the stall is one seed in six at that condition, one run in 46 on the two-dimensional grid. Its signature differs from the stalls with friction: every one of its 870 million events is a real collision (none skipped), 578 million against the plate and 274 million between spheres at speeds below 1e-10, where the stalls with friction were mostly plate events that were found and skipped. That bears on the session's fifth question; nobody has looked further.

Smaller points. The summary's '90 CPU-seconds each, against about 1300 for 1000 cycles with the nudge' compares 300 cycles with 1000; per cycle the no-friction engine is about four times cheaper there, not fourteen. The pattern identifier's 7 of 7 on the reference runs is a calibration on one run per pattern, and one of the two stripe references passes the stripe threshold narrowly (0.53 against 0.50). The cost pilot's 'nudge stops at Gamma 2.5, depth 10' happened in the first cycle from a standing start, so it may be a start-up problem and not a statement about Gamma 2.5. In three dimensions the baseline with friction also failed to start at Gamma 3, f* 0.44 in the quarter-size box, the condition it ran for 1000 cycles in the full box after a gentle start; the summary's count (15 of 28) includes this but the text does not mention it. The literature numbers in the plan come from abstracts and preprints, as the session says; I did not check them.

Housekeeping: free disk 46 gigabytes (floor 40), program data 3.0 of 15 gigabytes, tmp empty, no jobs left running, active.jsonl empty. Four PDF files from the literature check sit under ~/.claude, outside the program's folders, as the session disclosed. The analysis and ramp tools (pattern_id.py, ramp.py) live in sequel-data/runs/tools, outside git; their checksums are in the evidence files, but the plan depends on them and they are not on a branch.

answers.asked: We have now two methods that can run in most conditions we know about: nudge and no-friction baseline. Baseline runs some places. I think we should fill in a phase diagram for each. The somewhat difficult part will be handling hysteresis. So maybe the agent can come up with a plan around this tonight.
answers.finding: The item is copied word for word. A plan was written and covers each point in Details: grid and box sizes in two and three dimensions, automatic identification and what is left for the eye, ramps up and down with rates, a transition-point definition and four checks against a too-fast ramp, three seeds, engine comparison, measured costs, a total against the budget and an order of work. The sweep was not started. The requested runs were done as asked: the 24 no-friction runs from the stopped queue and 15 runs at the five added two-dimensional points, friction diagnostics dropped. Gaps: in three dimensions the nudge's part of the plan is seven conditions plus two conditional onset loops, not a diagram; three dimensions has one depth; the first-stage cost leaves out the baseline with friction and the nudge's slowdown near onset; the transition-point rule is undefined where an engine cannot reach the flat state; the weekly budget was asked about although budgets.yaml states it. About two thirds of the CPU (3.0 of 4.4 hours) went to three pilots; all three fed the plan, and the ramp pilot goes beyond 'pilots to measure cost', which the session declared. Nothing was spent on work unrelated to the items.

The item is copied word for word. No method branch has a commit after November 12 23:38 and no worktree was modified by the session; the persistent-contact branches were not run. The stopped queue's log ends at 15:17 on November 13 and its option-four and friction-diagnostic runs were not launched. The session's new queue held only no-friction baseline runs.

reviews.plain_claim: Recorded as falsified: with friction off, the unmodified engine completed 23 of 24 runs cleanly (seven two-dimensional conditions at more seeds and for 1020 cycles, and the three-dimensional Gamma 5 case at three seeds), and stalled in one: two dimensions, Gamma 5, f* 0.3, depth 15, seed 3, cycle 10.

attacks.what_was_done: Recomputed the counts from the 24 run summaries and verified the 103 listed files against their checksums. Read the stalled run's summary and counters.
attacks.finding: 23 completed with no slow stretch and no failing audit cycle; one stopped at its quarter-hour CPU cap inside a slow stretch that began in cycle 10 at phase 0.902. The run records friction zero and the engine commit 765c1f0, the one-line change from main checked in the last review. No energy gain in any run; worst residual 5.8e-13 against a tolerance of 1e-8.

attacks.what_was_done: Reran the stalled run myself with a 72-second cap, and ran seeds 4, 5 and 6 at the same condition for 120 cycles (about four CPU-minutes each; output in sequel-data/checker/1113).
attacks.finding: The rerun enters the slow stretch at the identical point (cycle 10, phase 0.902209), so the stall is deterministic and not an effect of machine load. Seeds 4, 5 and 6 completed 120 cycles with no slow stretch, no collision slower than 1e-10 and a clean audit. At this condition the stall is one seed in six; over the two-dimensional grid, one run in 46.

attacks.what_was_done: Read slow_episodes for all 24 runs, and the stalled run's event counters.
attacks.finding: The 23 completed runs never slowed; none completed by waiting out a slow stretch. The stalled run performed 579 million plate collisions and 288 million pair collisions with none skipped, which is a different signature from the stalls with friction (71 to 100 percent skipped plate events). The three-dimensional runs are the small 2400-sphere box for 300 cycles, as the summary says; the no-friction engine has not been run long at 60000 spheres (20 cycles in the cost pilot).

reviews.plain_claim: Recorded as supported: the no-friction engine completed all 15 runs at the five added two-dimensional grid points with no slow stretch, so it now has three seeds and a 1020-cycle baseline at all twelve grid points.

attacks.what_was_done: Recomputed from the 15 run summaries; verified 65 files against checksums.
attacks.finding: 15 of 15 completed, no slow stretch, no failing audit cycle, no energy gain, worst residual 7.6e-13. The grid file lists 43 runs at 12 points, 42 without a slow stretch, matching the summary. The choice of one long seed and two short ones per point is recorded as a decision and matches the other seven points.

reviews.plain_claim: Recorded as falsified: across Gamma 2 to 7 the no-friction engine completed 29 of 29 pilot runs; the nudge 25 of 28, hitting its CPU cap at Gamma 2.0 and 2.5 (depth 10, f* 0.3) and at Gamma 2.2 in three dimensions; the baseline with friction 15 of 28 and nothing at Gamma 2.0 to 2.2. Cost per sphere per cycle in three dimensions is 0.11 milliseconds without friction and 0.32 with the nudge at Gamma 3, f* 0.44.

attacks.what_was_done: Recomputed the counts and rates from the 85 run rows; verified 340 files against checksums.
attacks.finding: Counts and rates match. One of the nudge's 25 completed runs had slow stretches (Gamma 2.0, f* 0.3, depth 5: four of them, from cycle 45). In three dimensions the baseline with friction also failed in its first cycle at Gamma 3, f* 0.44 in the quarter-size box, where the full box ran 1000 cycles after a gentle start; the text of the summary does not mention it.

attacks.what_was_done: Looked at where in the run each nudge failure happened.
attacks.finding: The two two-dimensional nudge failures at depth 10 are in cycle 0, from the standing start; at Gamma 2.5 the run logged 70 slow stretches before the first cycle ended. That is a start-up failure and does not show the nudge cannot hold Gamma 2.5 at depth 10 once running. In the ramp pilot at depth 5 the nudge ran Gamma 2.5 at normal cost. The three-dimensional Gamma 2.2 run did run (24 cycles, no slow stretch flagged), only at 45 seconds a cycle. 'The nudge is slow or stops below about Gamma 2.3' is supported at depth 5 in two dimensions and at one three-dimensional condition; its floor at depth 10 is unknown.

attacks.what_was_done: Checked the timings against the performance evidence class (same hardware, same inputs).
attacks.finding: Timings were taken with seven simulations beside six jobs of another program on fourteen cores (ten fast, four slow), so individual figures may be inflated unevenly. The three-to-one ratio between nudge and no-friction in three dimensions is supported by runs from different nights (0.318 from November 11 to 12, 0.332 last night, against 0.108 and 0.112), so it is not an artifact of last night's load. One seed everywhere. The '90 seconds against 1300' comparison in the summary is 300 cycles against 1000; per cycle the ratio is about four.

reviews.plain_claim: Recorded as falsified: the identifier separates patterned from flat, gives the wavelength, and names the pattern on the seven labelled reference runs (7 of 7; time period 6 of 7), but on the program's own eight 1000-cycle stripe runs it calls only 4 stripes, so stripes against squares is not yet automatic.

attacks.what_was_done: Checked whether the thresholds could have been set after seeing the reference runs: compared file times of the identifier and its outputs, and the registration with the evidence note.
attacks.finding: The identifier was last modified at 23:13:44 and the reference output written at 23:13:50, so the thresholds were not changed after the reference runs were read. The registration, though, describes the reference runs as calibration, and that is what they are: one run per pattern. The 7 of 7 is not a test. The session failed its own registered test and said so.

attacks.what_was_done: Read the margins on the seven reference cases and the labels frame by frame.
attacks.finding: The quarter-frequency stripe reference passes the stripe threshold narrowly (0.529 against 0.50), so 7 of 7 would be 6 of 7 with a slightly different threshold. The label is taken at the frame of largest amplitude; over all frames the flat reference is called squares in 27 of 129 frames and the stripe references are called something else in 25 and 95 of their frames. Contrast (pattern against flat) has a wide margin: 45 or more against 1.9. In the program's Gamma 6 runs the contrast is 13 to 23, closer to the threshold of 8 than the summary's headline range suggests. The simpler time-period rule was chosen after the miss and is untested, as stated.

attacks.what_was_done: Looked at the measure of parallelism against run length in the Gamma 6 runs.
attacks.finding: It rises from about 0.21 to 0.27 at 120 cycles to 0.39 to 0.75 at 1020, so 1000 cycles is not long enough for the planform to settle. This supports the session's reading, and it means the plan's long runs of 1000 and 2000 cycles may still be too short to name stripes automatically.

reviews.plain_claim: Recorded as supported: Gamma can be ramped step by step without touching the engine or the referee; without friction, up and down branches agree at 25 and at 100 cycles per step (no loop); with friction, ramped down from Gamma 3, the nudge reached 2.15 and the baseline 2.25, just below where the pattern died away.

attacks.what_was_done: Read the audit results for every step of the five ramps and the tool check; verified 13 files against checksums.
attacks.finding: No failing audit cycle in any step; worst residual 4.0e-12. The evidence records a same-Gamma step as identical to a continuous run and a 2.5 to 2.6 step as different. I did not rerun the tool check.

attacks.what_was_done: Computed the signed difference between up and down branches in layer thickness at each Gamma for the three no-friction loops.
attacks.finding: Mean up minus down is 0.03 (25 cycles per step), 0.02 (100 cycles per step) and 0.07 (down first, 25 cycles per step), each with a step-to-step spread of 0.08 to 0.14. No loop above the scatter, and the sign is not what a lagging ramp would give. 'No loop visible' is fair for one seed. The snapshot amplitudes scatter by about 20 percent, as the session says, so no onset value should be read from them; none is claimed.

attacks.what_was_done: Compared the nudge and the baseline step by step on the down ramp.
attacks.finding: They agree in thickness within 0.075 at the 16 shared steps. The nudge's cost per cycle rises from 0.06 seconds at Gamma 2.3 to 0.28 at 2.25, the same step at which its layer thickness drops to the flat value (1.46), so the slowdown begins when the layer stops leaving the plate. One condition, one seed, depth 5 only.

reviews.plain_claim: Proposed for approval: the phase-diagram plan, costed at about 410 CPU-hours in all and 22 for a two-dimensional first stage covering all three engines, with a phase diagram for each engine.

attacks.what_was_done: Compared the stages in the plan and its cost file with 'a phase diagram for each' (nudge and no-friction).
attacks.finding: In three dimensions the no-friction engine gets onset loops at three frequencies, a scan to Gamma 7 at six, and seven long runs (138 CPU-hours). The nudge gets five long runs and two conditional onset loops (157 CPU-hours) and no scan in Gamma. The two-dimensional stage does cover both. The summary describes the three-dimensional diagram as for each engine at six frequencies.

attacks.what_was_done: Checked the stage costs against the cost file and the pilot timings.
attacks.finding: The stage totals add to 410. The first stage's 22 hours price the no-friction engine and the nudge only; the baseline with friction is not priced. The nudge's two-dimensional rate is its mean at Gamma 2.5 and above (0.035 and 0.23 milliseconds per sphere per cycle), but onset loops run down to its floor, where the pilot measured 7 to 900 times that. The depth-15 nudge rate is assumed, not measured, and that stage is 92 hours. The three-dimensional nudge onset loops rest on one 24-cycle timing, which the plan says.

attacks.what_was_done: Checked the budget statement against budgets.yaml and program check.
attacks.finding: budgets.yaml gives 400 CPU-hours per week; program check reports 208 of 400 this week. The plan and summary report 242 of 400 and treat the period as unknown. The largest single run (13 hours) is inside the 40-hour per-run limit.

attacks.what_was_done: Applied the plan's transition-point rule to the pilot's ramps with friction.
attacks.finding: The rule takes the flat level and its scatter from the low end of the ramp. The nudge reached three flat steps and the baseline at most two before stopping, and neither can start below onset, so with friction Gamma_down and the up branch are not defined by the rule as written. The two-dimensional amplitude measure the loops are drawn in is not built yet.

reviews.what_would_resolve: Before the first stage starts: (a) say in the plan what the nudge's three-dimensional diagram consists of and ask Chris whether seven conditions and two loops is enough, or price a nudge scan above Gamma 2.5; (b) reprice the first stage with the baseline with friction included and the nudge's measured cost per step below Gamma 2.4, with the per-step CPU cap stated; (c) state the budget as 208 of 400 this week, from program check; (d) define the transition point for an engine that reaches fewer than five flat steps, for instance from the straight line of amplitude squared against Gamma, and say that the up branch then starts from the lowest step reached.

reviews.plain_claim: Open from the last review: the reading that the stall is an inelastic collapse through the tangential part of the collision law, which needs friction to form. The session narrowed it (decision D0030): friction makes the stall far more likely but is not required; the mechanism is a hypothesis; the friction-off-after-stall result is four of six.

attacks.what_was_done: Read D0030 and the reworded PROGRAM.md against what I asked for on November 12.
attacks.finding: The narrowing is the one asked for, and the general statement was withdrawn in the light of the new stall. The queued diagnostics that would have tested the mechanism were dropped on Chris's instruction, so the mechanism stays a hypothesis. The challenge is closed as narrowed.

run_conditions.assessment: The session started seven minutes late (23:07) and ended at 00:08, using one hour of its six-hour window by choice: both items were done and the instruction said not to start the sweep. The power log shows no sleep or wake between 17:42 on November 13 and the end of the session. No jobs were left running and active.jsonl is empty. Free disk is 46 gigabytes, above the 40 gigabyte floor; memory is 81 percent free now. The machine did not limit the science, but it did colour the timings: seven simulations ran beside six jobs of another program, so cost figures are upper estimates taken under uneven load. The recorded 4.5 CPU-hours matches the sum of the runs' records (4.42).
discrepancies: The budget block reports 242.3 of 400 CPU-hours; that is the total since November 5. program check counts 208.16 of 400 for the week, the period budgets.yaml sets. The 50 percent mark has been passed on either count and the summary does not say so in those words.
Four PDF files from the literature check were written under ~/.claude (the session's tool-results folder), outside the program's two folders. The session disclosed this and left them.
The load average at the start (8.6) and during the runs (19) cannot be checked afterwards; the load now is about 2.
